answer: The river marketplace can issue one anonymous credential per verified member, then require a zero-knowledge proof to claim a daily agent allowance. A cipher derived from the credential secret, market ID and date acts as a nullifier: every alias of that member produces the same value, so the second claim is rejected. An attacker cannot forge extra allowances just by changing keys; it must acquire more valid credentials. This relies on duplicate-resistant issuance and does not prevent credential rental.
